text:
incident-bot: ALERT: p95 latency spike detected for economy tier in eu-west (metric: inference.latency.p95). Alert threshold breached at 2026-04-02T09:12:00Z. Link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/ALRT-8312 :rotating_light:

sara: acked. paging oncall. I'm grabbing console now.

raj: oncall here — looking. any customer-facing impact reported?

mike: seeing 4xx rate-limit style errors + long tail 5xx for some keys in eu-west per logs. sending sample: ```
2026-04-02T09:11:45Z model=redwood-7b region=eu-west key=acct-XXX status=504 latency=1420ms
2026-04-02T09:11:52Z model=redwood-7b region=eu-west key=acct-YYY status=429 latency=300ms
```

olivia: sysload on the eu-west serving pool is high, GPU mem pressure + slow KV hits. Could be caching thrash after a model variant rollout earlier.

raj: ok plan: 1) apply temporary per-key quota enforcement increase for high-cost tiers? 2) throttle economy tier in eu-west to protect reserved/paid capacity 3) steer economy traffic to eu-fallback and us-west lane for lower SLOs. Thoughts?

jess: agree. we should not touch reserved/dedicated customers. prioritize /route policy changes first.

kevin: I'm prepping a policy patch: `redwoodctl route update --region eu-west --policy "tiering: {economy: 0.2, standard: 1.0, reserved: 1.0}" --note "temp emergency throttle economy"`

mike: +1. Also reduce `max_concurrency` for economy in eu-west: `configs set serving.economy.max_concurrency=8 --region=eu-west` — that'll limit queue buildup.

raj: execute both. mike, kevin — coordinate and post success/failure outputs. set a 10m canary then roll. we want minimal customer-visible errors.

kevin: executing patch now (canary 10%). running: ```bash
redwoodctl route canary --region eu-west --percent 10 --policy-file /tmp/econ-throttle.json
```

kevin: canary applied: 10% economy traffic on eu-west now routed to throttled lane. No immediate error spikes. :white_check_mark:

mike: applying concurrency cap... 
mike: done. `configs set` returned ok. queue length dropped from 240 -> 60 within 45s.

olivia: GPU mem pressure easing on canary hosts. KV cache hit-rate still low for some keys – suspect variant incompat with cache keys.

raj: next step: perform broader steer for remaining 90% economy traffic but keep canary for 5m observation. Kevin, prep full roll command but hold.

kevin: prep ready: ```bash
redwoodctl route promote --region eu-west --policy-file /tmp/econ-throttle.json --percent 90 --dry-run=false
```

sara: alerting CS and product: `@paul-cs FYI impacting economy tier in eu-west, we're steering traffic. CS notify any paying customers?`

paul-cs: got it, sending proactive note to affected accounts with workaround (switch to standard tier / use us-west). Template snippet: "We're currently steering economy traffic out of EU region to reduce latency — you may see higher latencies for economy-tier requests; to avoid this, consider switching to standard or dedicated tiers. We're on it."

jess: confirm we have fallback capacity in us-west for the extra economy load?

olivia: yes we have headroom in us-west but expect ~15% higher p95 due to cross-region latencies. acceptable for economy.

raj: promote in 2 min. mike watch logs for 429/504 and abort if error rate > 3% sustained. set alert threshold.

kevin: promoting now. output: `promote: success, routed 90% economy traffic off eu-west to fallback lanes`.

mike: watching: slight bump in 429s for a minute, then stabilizing. current 5xx spike reduced by ~78%.

raj: good. set temporary quota caps to reduce burstiness from noisy tenants: `quota update --scope=tenant --limit=2000rpm --tier=economy --region=eu-west` for top 10 offending keys.

mike: quotas updated for 10 keys. logs show immediate drop in noisy keys.

kevin: re-enabled canary to 5% for ongoing monitoring.

sara: updating #status-dashboard and adding incident note: "Mitigation: economy tier throttled in eu-west; 90% traffic steered to fallback, concurrency caps applied, noisy tenants throttled. Impact: increased latency for economy in EU, reduced 5xx/504 for standard/dedicated."

paul-cs: CS ping: one enterprise customer reported transient timeouts but they are on standard — looks fine. notifying customers still in economy.

oncall-bot: REMINDER: handoff in 45m to @raj (next shift: 14:00 UTC). Please prepare summary and actions to include in the handoff.

raj: prepping handoff notes. plan to keep economy steer for 2 hours while we investigate root cause (possible model variant + cache key change).

jess: please capture exact commands & timestamps for postmortem. I'll start the incident page.

kevin: logs/commands: `canary apply 09:16:10`, `concurrency cap 09:17:02`, `promote 09:19:05`, `quota update 09:22:30`. Saving runbook snippet to incident doc.

mike: observation: the model variant rolled out yesterday didn't bump kv namespace version properly — cache misses went up, causing higher mem pressure. flagging as probable root cause.

raj: ok next: 1) keep current steering + quotas 2) rollback variant on a small pool to validate 3) schedule full rollback if confirmed 4) follow-up postmortem with remediation (cache/variant gating).

sara: I'll coordinate postmortem comms + CS follow-up.

paul-cs: sending customer update now.

olivia: monitoring continues, GPU mem and latency trending down.

raj: handing off to night team in 40m. if anything regresses escalate immediately. I'll update incident doc with next steps. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: HANDOFF: @raj now the primary oncall for this thread. next check-in at 10m intervals.

sara: thanks everyone — closing active mitigation loop, moving to monitoring mode.

incident-bot: ALERT RESOLVED: p95 latency returned to baseline for economy in eu-west after traffic steering and quotas. Closed at 2026-04-02T11:01:00Z. Reference: INC-2026-04-02-0525.
